Store layer

Source: R/io-store.R
io-store.Rd

The backend-neutral layer between the encodings and a storage format. Encodings (R/io-*.R) never call rhdf5 directly, they call the functions here, which dispatch on the class of the handle they are given to a backend (store_backend()). HDF5 (h5_backend()) and zarr (zarr_backend(), which writes v3 only so far) each have a list of the same operations.

Usage

node_path(node)

elem_path(store, key)

is_store_file(store)

node_open(store, path)

node_close(node)

group_create(store, key)

is_group(node)

group_members(node)

member_exists(store, key)

member_delete(store, key)

attr_exists(node, name)

attr_write(node, name, value, dtype = NULL, scalar = TRUE)

array_info(store, path)

array_read(store, path, selection = NULL, call = rlang::caller_env())

null_write(store, key)

table_write(
  store,
  key,
  frame,
  dataset_kwargs = list(),
  call = rlang::caller_env()
)

table_read(store, path, call = rlang::caller_env(), records = FALSE)

read_elem_attr(elem, name)

set_elem_attr(elem, name, value)

Arguments

store, node

An open file or group handle.

key, name

Name of a member of store, or of an attribute.

path

Absolute path of an Element or array.

value

The value to write.

dtype

The On-disk dtype of an attribute, NULL for the type of value.

scalar

Whether a character vector is written as a scalar. Character vectors are written as variable-length UTF-8, logicals as scalars and dtype = "int64" writes an int64 array.

selection

A selection, see the description.

call

The call reported by errors.

frame

A data frame of numeric, logical and character columns.

dataset_kwargs

A list of dataset creation options.

records

Whether table_read() records the field dtypes (HDF5 only, zarr always does).

Details

A store is an open file or group, and a node is an open group or array. Both are handles of the backend, and paths are absolute within the store.

A selection is NULL (the whole array) or a list with one entry per dimension, each NULL (every index) or a strictly increasing vector of 1-based indices. Dimensions are in Python's order, so selection = list(1:2, NULL) is numpy's x[0:2, :].

The array information from array_info() is a one-row data frame, as h5ls() gives, with name, dclass (INTEGER, FLOAT, ENUM, COMPOUND or STRING), dtype and rank, and the list columns shape and chunks (numeric vectors in Python's order). chunks is NULL for a contiguous HDF5 dataset and for a 0-d array, and the inner chunk shape for a sharded zarr array.
